title: The indexing nerve inclusion of a directed simplicial cover is right anodyne
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and ordinary nerves of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and right anodyne maps of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. Thus a right anodyne map is in the smallest class containing all isomorphisms and all horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0<i\leq n$, closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set and $I$ a small nonempty partially ordered set in which every finite subset has an upper bound. Let $(K_a)_{a\in I}$ be simplicial subsets of $K$, with $K_a\subseteq K_b$ when $a\leq b$ and $\bigcup_a K_a=K$. Define a simplicial set $K_F$ by
$$ (K_F)_n=K_n\amalg N(I)_n\amalg\coprod_{0\leq i<n}\coprod_{a_{i+1}\leq\cdots\leq a_n}(K_{a_{i+1}})_i. $$
A mixed simplex has an initial $i$-simplex $\sigma$ in $K_{a_{i+1}}$ and a final chain of indices. Operators restrict or repeat these two ordered blocks. On the lower block they act on $\sigma$; on the upper block they act on the chain. If the first upper index is deleted, regard $\sigma$ in the next subset by inclusion. If the entire upper block disappears, retain $\sigma$ in $K$; if the entire lower block disappears, retain the chain in $N(I)$. These rules also specify the pure $K$ and pure nerve simplices and their inclusions.
Then the inclusion $N(I)\hookrightarrow K_F$ is right anodyne. Neither $K$ nor any $K_a$ is required to be a quasicategory, and no cone structure on any $K_a$ is required.

source.place: HTT Proposition 4.2.3.8 and Remark 4.2.3.9, printed pp. 252-253, specialized to an increasing directed cover by simplicial subsets; Notation 4.2.3.1 for K_F. Online text read 2026-10-17; archive WANTED. These are infinity-categorical facts; no Stacks tag states them.

proof.text: Let $H$ be the simplicial subset of the displayed degreewise construction consisting of the pure $K$ and $N(I)$ simplices and of the mixed simplices whose lower simplex $\sigma$ lies in $K_{a_{i+1}}$. The face and degeneracy operators on a lower block act inside that simplicial subset. Operators on the upper chain preserve its order; when the first upper index is deleted, the new first index is larger and the inclusion $K_{a_{i+1}}\subseteq K_{a_{i+2}}$ carries $\sigma$ to the required lower block. If the upper block disappears, the pure $K$ summand remains, and if the lower block disappears the pure nerve summand remains. Thus the stated formulas define a simplicial set $H=K_F$ and the evident inclusion $N(I)\hookrightarrow H$.

source.place: Notation 4.2.3.1 and the simplicial-operator rules for K_F; direct verification in the specialized increasing-cover case

proof.text: For every nondegenerate simplex $\sigma$ of $K$, put $I_\sigma=\{a\in I\mid \sigma\in K_a\}$ with the induced order. It is nonempty because the $K_a$ cover $K$. If $a,b\in I_\sigma$, an upper bound $c$ for $\{a,b\}$ lies in $I_\sigma$ because the family is increasing. Hence $I_\sigma$ is a small nonempty directed poset; its parallel arrows are equal. The statement of [lem-cbc-filtered-nerve-weak-contractibility] therefore applies and gives $N(I_\sigma)\to\Delta^0$ a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.8, directed-index verification for the subposets of indices containing a simplex; weak contractibility input

proof.text: Well-order the nondegenerate simplices of $K$ by increasing dimension, so that every face of a simplex comes before it, and for an initial collection $L$ let $H(L)$ contain all of $N(I)$, the pure simplices of $K$ whose nondegenerate root lies in $L$, and exactly the mixed simplices whose lower simplex has its nondegenerate root in $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition], every simplex $\tau$ of $K$ is uniquely $S(s)(\rho)$ for a surjection $s$ and a nondegenerate root $\rho$; since each $K_a$ is a simplicial subset, $\tau\in K_a$ if and only if $\rho\in K_a$. As faces of $\rho$ have roots of smaller dimension, each $H(L)$ is a simplicial subset. Starting with $H(\varnothing)=N(I)$, adjoining a nondegenerate $m$-simplex $\sigma$ is the pushout of $\partial\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)$ along the map sending a pure simplex $\alpha$ of $\Delta^m$ to $S(\alpha)(\sigma)$, a chain to itself, and a mixed pair $(\alpha,a_{i+1}\leq\cdots\leq a_n)$ to $(S(\alpha)(\sigma),a_{i+1}\leq\cdots\leq a_n)$, which lies in $K_F$ because $\sigma\in K_{a_{i+1}}$. The boundary part lands in the old stage, because the faces of $\sigma$ come earlier. The simplices of $\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)$ outside $\partial\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)$ are those whose $\Delta^m$ part is a surjection $s$ onto $[m]$. By the uniqueness of the decomposition they correspond bijectively to the new simplices: the pure degeneracies $S(s)(\sigma)$, and the mixed simplices with lower simplex $S(s)(\sigma)$ and first index in $I_\sigma$. Their whole chain then lies in $I_\sigma$, since $I_\sigma$ is upward closed. Hence the square is a pushout degreewise. Unlike the plain relative skeletal filtration of [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], which attaches all cells of one dimension in a single coproduct, this is a transfinite sequence of single attachments. At a limit stage, the union is $H(L)$ for the union of the earlier collections.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.8, filtration of K_F by nondegenerate simplices and its pushout description; Proposition 4.2.3.1 notation

proof.text: By step 2, $N(I_\sigma)\to\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-contractible-join-right-anodyne] to $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ and $N(I_\sigma)$; it says that each attaching map $\partial\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)$ is right anodyne, with no quasicategory hypothesis on either factor. The sequence in step 3 is obtained by pushouts of these maps, including the successive pushouts used to refine any coproduct of cells, and its limit is their transfinite composite. Closure under pushouts and small transfinite compositions, which is part of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne], therefore makes the composite $N(I)=H(\varnothing)\hookrightarrow H(K)=K_F$ right anodyne. The empty-dimensional case uses $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$ and is included.
